findings.claim: sellbird-routes.yaml contains no passthrough route for Kratos self-service, although the change's own acceptance text names "passthrough for Kratos self-service routes" as content of that exact file.
findings.evidence: acceptance_criteria (sellbird-gateway-route-config/proposal.md, Why and What Changes): "Write infra/flint-gate/sellbird-routes.yaml: kratos_session auth, a claims_enhancement hook minting an RS256 JWT with aud=sellbird and TTL of 300 s or less, passthrough for Kratos self-service routes, and no admin-port exposure." vs the file's own header, line 15: "#   - the auth host's routes (Kratos self-service passthrough, login UI);" listed under "Everything else in config.yaml is platform-owned and deliberately absent here". The file ships only sites:[sellbird] and routes:[sellbird-api, sellbird-dashboard], both of which require kratos_session plus a verified gate JWT, so no self-service path exists anywhere in the delivered config.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the auth-host site and Kratos self-service passthrough routes to sellbird-routes.yaml as the proposal states, or change the proposal/acceptance wording to say the auth host is platform-owned and record that as an explicit contract dependency so the deliverable is not silently redefined in a README comment.

findings.claim: Kratos's public base_url is http:// while every other URL in the same file is https://, so the stand-in generates cleartext self-service flow URLs and a session cookie whose Secure flag follows a non-TLS scheme.
findings.evidence: kratos.yml line 25 `base_url: http://auth.example.test/` vs `default_browser_return_url: https://sellbird.example.test/`, `allowed_return_urls: - https://sellbird.example.test/`, `flows.error.ui_url: https://auth.example.test/error`, `flows.login.ui_url: https://auth.example.test/login`, `flows.settings.ui_url: https://auth.example.test/settings` (all https). Kratos derives absolute self-service URLs and cookie security from `serve.public.base_url`, and the file header claims it "mirrors the settings the platform contract requires" for a TLS-terminated Gateway.
findings.suggested_fix: Set `serve.public.base_url: https://auth.example.test/` so flow URLs and cookie flags match the https scheme used everywhere else in the file.

findings.claim: The "pinned JWKS" may be fetched over plain http, so an on-path attacker between Sellbird and flint-gate can substitute signing keys and forge tokens that pass every verification check.
findings.evidence: config.py `_jwks_url`: `if parts.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parts.hostname:` — both schemes accepted, documented as "the pinned JWKS location (http or https, no credentials)". jwks.py `fetch_jwks` then does a plain `client.stream("GET", url, ...)` with no TLS or key-pinning requirement. Acceptance criterion "Gate token verification" requires admission "only with a flint-gate JWT that verifies against the pinned JWKS with the expected issuer, audience, key id and algorithm"; a JWKS retrieved over an unauthenticated channel is not pinned against substitution, and `sellbird.auth.gate_token` trusts whatever `JwksCache` returns for `kid`.
findings.suggested_fix: Require https for SELLBIRD_GATE_JWKS_URL, or (if in-cluster http is deliberate) pin the JWKS response by an expected signing-key thumbprint and document the network-trust boundary in config.py rather than silently permitting cleartext.

findings.claim: add_feedback now runs the full schema initialisation on every dashboard POST and relies on StateManager.add_feedback's return value, replacing the previous lightweight create-table-if-missing plus id generation.
findings.evidence: dashboard.py hunk @@ -825,25 +834,11 @@: removed `feedback_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS feedback (...)` and the direct INSERT; added `state = _state()` / `await state.init_db()` / `feedback_id = await state.add_feedback(...)`. The removed comment said the inline DDL existed "so feedback works even on a fresh install"; that property now depends on `init_db()` succeeding, and the unchanged `except Exception as e: ... return {"success": False, "message": "Could not save feedback."}` turns any missing/non-async `add_feedback` or migration failure into a generic client message with only a warning log (silent failure), while `init_db()` mutates the schema from a request path and is paid on every submission.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep schema creation out of the request path (run init_db at startup) and assert/return the id explicitly; if `add_feedback` can return None, generate the id before the call rather than assuming the return value is the new id.

findings.claim: `del url` in the container branch is a fragile suppression that raises NameError if any later statement in start_dashboard references url, and it leaves the Windows footer printed after "Press Ctrl+C to stop."
findings.evidence: dashboard.py hunk @@ -2990,9 +3044,16 @@: `if running_in_container(): ... del url ... print("  Press Ctrl+C to stop.\n")` followed by `if os.name == "nt": print("  Windows: ...")` which runs in both branches, so the container path prints the stop message before the Windows note. The suppression only needs the value not to be printed, not deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `del url` and simply omit it from the container message (e.g. `del` nothing; keep `url` unused), and move the Windows note inside the non-container branch or before the stop message.
